record.context_brief: Necessity of supercoercivity in near-Chebyshev single-valuedness
record.original_question: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and let C be a nonempty closed subset of U. Suppose f is twice continuously differentiable and the Hessian grad^2 f(y) is positive definite for every y in U. Fact 3.5 says that if f is also supercoercive, then the left nearest-point map P_left,C is single-valued almost everywhere and generically on U. Is that extra supercoercivity assumption really essential for the almost-everywhere and generic single-valuedness conclusion?

evidence.quote: Fact 3.5 (See [7, Corollary 5.6].) Suppose that f is supercoercive, that f is twice continuously differentiable, and that for every y in U, grad^2 f(y) is positive definite. Then <-PC is almost everywhere and generically single-valued on U.
It would be interesting to see whether or not supercoercivity is essential in Fact 3.5.
Problem 5. Is the assumption that f be supercoercive in Fact 3.5 really essential?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X=\mathbb{R}^n$ with its standard Euclidean inner product. A proper convex lower semicontinuous function $f:X\to[-\infty,+\infty]$ is called Legendre if it is both essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex; equivalently, $f$ is differentiable on $U:=\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom} f\neq\varnothing$, $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to\infty$ whenever $x_k\to x\in\operatorname{bdry}\operatorname{dom} f$, and $f$ is strictly convex on $U$. The function $f$ is called supercoercive if $\lim_{\|x\|\to\infty} f(x)/\|x\|=+\infty$. The associated Bregman distance is
$$D_f(x,y)=f(x)-f(y)-\langle \nabla f(y),x-y\rangle\quad\text{for }x\in\operatorname{dom} f,\ y\in U,$$
and for a nonempty closed set $C\subseteq U$ the left Bregman nearest-point map is
$$\overleftarrow{P}_{\!C}(y)=\operatorname{argmin}_{c\in C} D_f(c,y),\qquad y\in U.$$
A map $T:U\rightrightarrows X$ is said to be single-valued almost everywhere on $U$ if the set of $y\in U$ at which $T(y)$ is not a singleton has Lebesgue measure zero, and single-valued generically on $U$ if this exceptional set is meager (a countable union of nowhere dense sets).

It is known that if, in addition to being Legendre, $f$ is twice continuously differentiable on $U$, the Hessian $\nabla^2 f(y)$ is positive definite for every $y\in U$, and $f$ is supercoercive, then $\overleftarrow{P}_{\!C}$ is single-valued almost everywhere and generically on $U$ for every nonempty closed $C\subseteq U$.

Question: Is the supercoercivity hypothesis necessary for this conclusion? Equivalently, does there exist a Legendre function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ that is twice continuously differentiable on $U=\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom} f$ with positive definite Hessian everywhere on $U$, but not supercoercive, together with a nonempty closed set $C\subseteq U$, for which $\overleftarrow{P}_{\!C}$ fails to be single-valued almost everywhere or generically on $U$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for follow-up work on this question (concerning the necessity of supercoercivity in the almost-everywhere and generic single-valuedness of the left Bregman nearest-point map for Legendre functions with positive definite Hessian) did not turn up a definitive resolution. Related works by Bauschke and collaborators on Bregman distances and Chebyshev sets are available, but none clearly settles whether supercoercivity is essential here.
